note: v1, written: SECOND STREAM. Deep dub techno at 124 bpm in D minor (the style board's t8 row). A 909 kick whose tail feeds a pumped RUMBLE bus (a hall, low-passed at 170 Hz and driven), the sub on the off-beats, open hats on every off-beat, and closed 16ths accented every fifth - doubled by a metal hat on the accents, FIVE OVER FOUR walking across the bar. A song-local DUB CHORD stab (D minor 9, mutating by phrase: Dm9 -> Dm11 -> Bb and Gm colours) on the and-of-one goes into THE ROOM, a feedback echo chamber (3/16 delay -> 1.9 kHz low-pass -> tape, fed back at 0.74). STREAM SPLIT: the dry stab sinks while the room's send rises, so in the break - no kick, the hall frozen - the dotted-eighth echoes are the loudest rhythm left and the ear takes them as the beat, until the kick slams back in B. Form: intro 16, build 16 (a Shepard riser into A), A 32, break 16, B 32 (the ride), peak 16 (claps), outro 16 - 4:43. The master is pushed to the album's louder target (rms -14.6, crest 8.4). compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: 88.238/88.445/88.321/88.734.
next: rhythm 58 (off-grid 0.01: the echo stream needs to read as its own pulse in the A and B sections too); density cv 0.10; rms -14.6 (target -14..-6).

note: v2, written: THE ECHO'S GRID, PLAYED. Through A, B and the peak the 909 rim now plays every third 16th: a dotted-eighth cycle running across the bar lines, three against the kick's four. It is the room's own echo time made a part, so the second stream lives in the drums as well as in the echoes, and the break's phantom downbeat has been set up by the groove before it (rhythm 58 -> 60). compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: v1 88.238/88.445/88.321/88.734 -> v2 89.456/89.191/89.108/89.201. next: rhythm 60 (the kick's grid still dominates the autocorrelation); density cv; rms -14.6 (target -14..-6); a long-build / drop and an illusion moment (Harry's brief).

note: v3, written: THE PHANTOM DOWNBEAT. The break now carries the track's illusion. The off-beat open hats, the 4/4 grid's loudest marker, leave with the kick; only parts that fit both grids stay (the closed 16ths, back from the break's ninth bar). From its fifth bar the rim's 3/16 cycle returns, climbing in velocity under the room's echoes, so the dotted-eighth stream is the clearest pulse left and the ear takes it as the beat until B's kick snaps the grid back (rhythm 60 -> 65). compscore seeds 0/11/19/29 (v2 re-measured with flow now counted, t9 next door): v2 89.107/88.870/88.796/88.879 -> v3 89.526/89.912/89.555/89.537. note: v4, written: THE STAB BREATHES (Harry's note: better LFO use, odd lengths, movement that evolves; and restraint). The dub chord's low-pass now drifts on a 7-bar sine and a 5-bar triangle, its resonance on a 3-bar sine, and its place in the stereo field on a 5-bar sine. None of them lands with the 16-bar phrases, so the loop is never quite the same twice. A section lane opens it across the arc: dark in the intro, opening through A, darkest in the break, brightest at the peak. Restraint: the Shepard riser is gone (Shepard and Risset are No Floor's), leaving fewer parts, each doing more. compscore seeds 0/11/19/29 (v3 re-measured after Harry's ratings): v3 89.106/89.491/89.135/89.115 -> v4 91.461/91.051/90.679/91.300 (variety 84 -> 93-98). note: v5, written: THE KICK, ANALOG (after Harry's note to come closer to No Floor's drive and physicality). The four-on-the-floor moves to its own track on chirper-two's new machine-kit, the 909 circuit as a signal path (a swept VCO, a click and drive). It still feeds the rumble bus and keys every pump. The 909 keeps the hats, the rim, the claps and the ride, so the room and the grid sound as before and only the kick hits harder. The master reaches the album's loudness (rms -14.6 -> -14.05) and the rhythm term goes 65 -> 100.
